questions.stem: Why is gold often found as a pure metal in nature rather than in an ore?

options.text: Gold reacts with water but not with oxygen
Gold is very unreactive and does not combine with other elements easily
Gold is too heavy to form compounds
Gold is very reactive and breaks down ores easily

questions.explanation: Gold is at the bottom of the reactivity series, making it very unreactive. It does not react easily with oxygen, water, or other substances, so it remains as the pure element in nature rather than forming compounds in ores.
